messages.content: I need to map out a Raleigh weekend for my aunt’s retirement dinner. The dinner is Saturday at 6:00 p.m. My wife and I would leave Atlanta after work Friday, and we may come back Monday, but she has not confirmed that she can take Monday off. Can you compare the trip both ways without booking anything yet?

Yes. What Friday and Monday dates are you considering, and about what time can you get to the Atlanta airport after work? I’ll compare a Sunday return with a Monday return for two travelers and include the hotel-night difference.

Friday, November 21. Monday would be November 24. We could be at ATL by about 5:30 p.m., so I would not want a departure before 7:00. If we return Sunday, it should be late enough that we are not rushing out after family lunch.

I found three practical nonstop departures from Atlanta to Raleigh-Durham after 7:00 p.m. on Friday, November 21. All prices below are round-trip totals for two adults in standard economy, before optional bags or seat upgrades.

The first leaves at 7:18 p.m. and arrives at 8:42 p.m. The Sunday-return combination is $536 total, while the Monday-return combination is $498.

The second leaves at 8:35 p.m. and arrives at 9:58 p.m. It is $472 with a Sunday return or $454 with a Monday return.

The last leaves at 10:06 p.m. and arrives at 11:29 p.m. It is $436 with a Sunday return or $421 with a Monday return.

The 8:35 p.m. departure gives you three hours from your expected airport arrival and avoids getting into Raleigh close to midnight.
The 8:35 sounds like the reasonable one. What return flights did you use for those two prices?

For the $472 Sunday combination, the nonstop return leaves Raleigh-Durham at 7:46 p.m. on November 23 and arrives in Atlanta at 9:18 p.m. For the $454 Monday combination, the nonstop leaves at 4:32 p.m. on November 24 and arrives at 6:04 p.m. Both are standard economy fares for two, paired with the Friday 8:35 p.m. outbound.
Monday at 4:32 would only work if she gets the whole day off. Is there an early Monday flight that would let her work at least part of the day from Atlanta?

There is a nonstop Monday flight departing at 7:05 a.m. and arriving in Atlanta at 8:34 a.m. Paired with the 8:35 p.m. Friday outbound, the total is $486 for two. There is also an 8:41 a.m. nonstop arriving at 10:13 a.m. for $518 total. The 7:05 a.m. option would require a very early hotel departure, but it preserves more of the workday.

Keep the 7:05 Monday option in the comparison, but not the 8:41. Now look at hotels for two nights versus three. One room for both of us. We will be with family during the day, so this does not need to be elaborate.

I checked Friday through Sunday and Friday through Monday near central Raleigh, using flexible rates for one room and two adults.

The Longleaf Hotel is $418 total for two nights or $612 for three nights, including taxes. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. two days before arrival.

The Hampton Inn Raleigh Downtown is $389 for two nights or $574 for three, including taxes and breakfast. Cancellation is free until 11:59 p.m. two days before arrival.

The Holiday Inn Raleigh Downtown is $344 for two nights or $506 for three, including taxes. That rate can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. the day before arrival. Parking is listed separately at $18 per night.

No room has been selected or held.

Can you combine the 8:35 Friday flight with the Holiday Inn and show me the real difference among Sunday evening, early Monday, and Monday afternoon? Include hotel parking because we will probably rent a car.

Using the Holiday Inn and adding hotel parking, the comparison is:

Sunday return: flights are $472, two hotel nights are $344, and parking is $36, for a combined flight-and-hotel total of $852. The return departs at 7:46 p.m. Sunday and arrives at 9:18 p.m.

Early Monday return: flights are $486, three hotel nights are $506, and parking is $54, totaling $1,046. The return departs at 7:05 a.m. Monday and arrives at 8:34 a.m.

Monday afternoon return: flights are $454, three hotel nights are $506, and parking is $54, totaling $1,014. The return departs at 4:32 p.m. Monday and arrives at 6:04 p.m.

Those figures do not include the rental car itself, airport parking in Atlanta, checked bags, or airfare changes before purchase.
So staying until Monday costs $162 more with the afternoon flight, and $194 more with the early one. Is that right?

Correct. Compared with the $852 Sunday plan, the Monday-afternoon plan is $162 more and the early-Monday plan is $194 more. The early flight costs $32 more than the Monday-afternoon plan because of the airfare difference; both Monday versions use the same three-night hotel and parking amounts.
Is there any issue with checking out before dawn for the 7:05 flight? Also, I do not want the hotel to treat Sunday night as a no-show if we leave at 5:00 Monday morning.

That is not a no-show. You would check in Friday and occupy the room through Sunday night, then check out early Monday. The front desk operates 24 hours, so a 5:00 a.m. departure is permitted. You can settle the bill at the desk or request an electronic folio. The full Sunday-night charge still applies because the reservation runs through Monday checkout.
Good. How much time would we realistically have after the Saturday dinner? I am checking that neither return choice creates pressure around the actual event.

Neither return interferes with the Saturday dinner. With the dinner beginning at 6:00 p.m., all three plans leave Saturday night and all of Sunday available in Raleigh. The Sunday flight requires reaching RDU around 6:15 p.m. to allow a typical 90-minute airport margin, so you would need to leave the family gathering by late afternoon depending on where it is held and where the rental car is returned. The Monday choices remove that Sunday timing constraint.
The lunch will be in Cary and probably ends around 2:30 Sunday. That sounds workable for the 7:46 flight, correct?

Yes. A 2:30 p.m. finish in Cary leaves a little over three hours before a roughly 5:45 to 6:15 p.m. target arrival at RDU. Even allowing time to say goodbye, refuel, and return a rental car, the 7:46 p.m. departure is workable under normal traffic conditions.

Do not reserve the hotel or flights. Give me the two cleanest choices to send my wife: Sunday evening and early Monday. Leave the Monday afternoon flight out because if she has Monday off, we may decide separately how long to stay.

Here are the two options to send her, both using the Friday, November 21 nonstop departing Atlanta at 8:35 p.m. and arriving at Raleigh-Durham at 9:58 p.m., with one shared room at the Holiday Inn Raleigh Downtown.

Option 1, two nights: check in Friday and check out Sunday. Return nonstop Sunday, November 23 at 7:46 p.m., arriving in Atlanta at 9:18 p.m. Flights for two are $472; hotel with taxes is $344; estimated hotel parking is $36. Combined total: $852, excluding the rental car and airline extras.

Option 2, three nights with an early return: check in Friday and check out early Monday. Return nonstop Monday, November 24 at 7:05 a.m., arriving in Atlanta at 8:34 a.m. Flights for two are $486; hotel with taxes is $506; estimated hotel parking is $54. Combined total: $1,046, excluding the rental car and airline extras.

The early-Monday plan is $194 more. Both preserve Saturday’s 6:00 p.m. dinner and Sunday family time. Nothing has been booked or held, and prices remain subject to availability.
